claims.claim: The paper reports that FiDo reduces MBI-Net+ RMSE from 26.10 to 24.11 and improves over the best 2023 Clarity Prediction Challenge system.
claims.limitations: Weakly supervised targets, hearing-aid/noise conditions, challenge split, proxy RMSE, and absence of a new listener study bound the claim; prediction is not equivalent to real-world access improvement.

claims.claim: The paper reports that the enhanced method reproduces durational accents observed in real L2 speech.
claims.limitations: Accent languages, speakers, duration estimator, perceptual validation, and native-corpus assumptions bound transfer; acoustic similarity is not proof of improved ASR or pedagogy.

claims.claim: The paper reports better results than standard diffusion baselines and GPU input-output latency around 0.3–1 seconds.
claims.limitations: GPU/hardware assumptions, buffer size, noise mixtures, real-time scheduling, and perceptual metrics bound the result; a reported latency range is not a full conversational user study.

claims.claim: On TED-LIUM2, the paper reports WER 7.3% for both the proposed and autoregressive systems, with RTF 0.41 versus 0.59.
claims.limitations: One corpus/model, beam and hardware settings, confidence thresholds, and real-time measurement protocol bound transfer; equal WER on one test set does not prove universal speed preservation.

claims.claim: The paper reports that FlowTSE matches or outperforms strong target-speaker-extraction baselines on standard benchmarks.
claims.limitations: Enrollment quality, speaker/noise shift, phase-vocoder design, benchmark mixtures, and signal metrics bound transfer; extraction quality is not automatically improved ASR or hearing-aid benefit.

claims.claim: The paper reports that its codec denoiser outperforms speech-enhancement baselines and that noise-robust LauraTTS improves over adding an external enhancer.
claims.limitations: Noise types, prompt duration, speaker overlap, codec/model version, and zero-shot evaluation bound transfer; clean synthesis from a prompt is not speaker-authenticated identity preservation.

claims.claim: MKL-VC reports improved content preservation and short-reference robustness on LibriSpeech and FLEURS, with cross-lingual performance comparable to FACodec.
claims.limitations: Reference duration, WavLM space, languages, vocoder, speaker similarity metric, and implementation choices bound transfer; content preservation does not prove perfect identity conversion.

claims.claim: Using 16 listeners and 180 Japanese speakers in J-AESOP, the paper reports greater leniency among some nonnative listeners and stronger fit for segment-based articulation rate.
claims.limitations: Listener sample, language backgrounds, trained-rating task, corpus, feature definitions, and Bayesian priors bound transfer; fluency ratings are not a complete measure of communicative success.
